text.p: A final draft of a reform to allow Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso the chance of a second term was read to a congressional panel on Tuesday, but voting will not take place until January, a deputy said.
A vote on the bill, which was scheduled to take place on Tuesday, was delayed when government leaders asked for more time to study the draft, part of their strategy for approval of the reform.
Dep. Benito Gama, the government's leader in the Chamber of Deputies, told reporters he expected the lower house committee would vote on the proposal around January 8.

Earlier, an aide to Gama said the government would delay the vote on the proposed constitutional amendment to prevent the opposition from doing likewise in January and stalling progress on the reform.

The final version of the amendment would enable presidents, state governors and mayors to stand for a second, consecutive term. A proposal that holders of executive office should stand down temporarily before running for re-election was not included in the draft.

Government leaders expect the amendment to be approved by the panel without difficulties. They are currently mustering support for the next, bigger hurdle -- two three-fifths majorities on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies.
